facts.text: Rupert sprang to life in 1906 when the Minidoka Dam finished, and it soon became one of the first cities worldwide to light its streets with electricity.
The Minidoka County Historical Museum displays restored railroad cars, early 1900s memorabilia, Native American artifacts, and a vintage steam engine that once powered the town.
Nestled on the edge of Rupert Square, the Wilson Theatre is a beautifully restored 1920s performance gem that still hosts live shows.
Rupert Square and its downtown streets are lined with welcoming shops, historic buildings, and cozy cafés that showcase the town’s small‑town charm.
As the county seat of Minidoka County, Rupert sits 3 miles northwest of the Snake River on the fertile Magic Valley plain.
Before it was named Rupert, the settlement was called “Wellfirst,” a nod to the first well that sparked early development.
